title: James Beard Foundation
about: The James Beard Foundation is a nonprofit that celebrates and supports the people behind America’s food culture. It was founded in 1986, the year after James Beard’s death, when his former student Peter Kump, encouraged by Julia Child, bought Beard’s Greenwich Village brownstone at 167 West 12th Street. Beard lived and taught there from 1973 until 1985, and the James Beard House has hosted guest-chef dinners since 1987, when Wolfgang Puck cooked the first.

Today the foundation’s work reaches well beyond the townhouse: the James Beard Awards, scholarships for culinary students, and programs built on its mission of “Good Food for Good,” anchored in talent, equity and sustainability. In New York it also runs Platform, its space in the Pier 57 food hall on the Hudson River.

On October 2 and 3, 2026, Eden hosted its first Friends of James Beard Benefit dinner. Guests began with a reception, then sat down to an eight-course tasting menu cooked over our wood-fired hearth, with optional wine pairings presented by sommelier Keenan Davis. Proceeds support the foundation’s programs for the restaurant community.
